problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨\text{_____},\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=3.$ What is the first component of $f?$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\text{_____}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=49.$ What is the third component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $7$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =7.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨7\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,7\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$ 

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $7\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$
